Myths on Clay retells the myths and legends of Bali in the style of Kamasan wayang painting. Some come from old Balinese palm-leaf books (lontar), some from royal chronicles, and some are folk tales told aloud for generations: we always say which is which. Balinese Hinduism is a living faith, and these stories are still told, danced and celebrated on the island today.
Sources: Usana Bali; Kuttara Kanda Dewa Purana Bangsul; Calon Arang (ed. R. Ng. Poerbatjaraka, 1926); Dwijendra Tattwa; Pararaton and Nagarakretagama (1365). Further reading: Miguel Covarrubias, Island of Bali (1937); Beryl de Zoete & Walter Spies, Dance and Drama in Bali (1938); Jane Belo, Bali: Rangda and Barong (1949); C. Hooykaas, Cosmogony and Creation in Balinese Tradition (1974); Fred B. Eiseman, Bali: Sekala and Niskala (1989); Adrian Vickers, Bali: A Paradise Created (1989).
Narrated by Matías.
